messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm onboarding icarus-6b-qat to the model catalog. Two quick things: where are the ONNX quantized weights stored (S3 path)? And I hit a tokenizer mismatch: sentences starting with \"Hello\" get an extra leading-space token compared to our baseline tokenizer. Can someone sanity-check config before I kick off perf runs?

sam: weights are in s3://redwood-models/icarus/6b/quant/onnx/v1/weights.tar.gz :eyes:  (we also have a v0 non-quant there)

maya: thanks. sam — do you know if that tar contains tokenizer.json or just model.onnx files?

sam: just onnx + metadata.json currently. tokenizer is in a separate repo: git@github.com:redwood/tokenizers.git under models/icarus/6b/tokenizer_v1/

devon: about the leading-space token — that's usually a vocab/normalization mismatch. Did you run the tokenizer with trim_offsets=false? Our python wrapper sets preserve_space=True by default, but the ONNX exporter expects legacy trimming sometimes.

maya: I used the catalog's export script: `python export_to_onnx.py --model icarus-6b --quant --export-tokenizer` — looks like export didn't include tokenizer. Export logs: "WARN: tokenizer not serialized, skipping"

arjun: that warning means the tokenizer failed a validation check (tokenizer_utils.vocab_checksum). Can you paste the metadata.json here?

maya: metadata snippet:
```
{
  "model": "icarus-6b",
  "onnx_version": "opset12",
  "quant": "int8_qat",
  "tokenizer_checksum": "missing",
  "max_seq_len": 2048
}
```

devon: ah — tokenizer_checksum missing. Exporter refuses to bundle tokenizer when checksum absent. That explains the leading-space differences. Two options: 1) pull tokenizer from tokenizers repo and provide checksum, or 2) regenerate tokenizer artifacts via `python tokenizers/build_tokenizer.py --model icarus-6b --output out/` and then update metadata.

maya: I'll pull the tokenizer dir and run build. Meanwhile, for perf runs: planning to benchmark latency and throughput for batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16] on a p4d-like instance. Any recommended flags? Should I enable continuous batching in the config or keep it off for baseline?

devon: baseline = continuous_batching OFF. Measure p50/p99 and tokens/sec. Then enable continuous batching and autoscale_batch to see impact. Also try kv_cache_pinning=true for chat-like workloads.

arjun: watch out for the sequence length handling — ONNX exporter currently pads to multiples of 16 if pad_alignment=16 in runtime config. That kills tail latency for short inputs. Set pad_alignment=1 for the latency-focused runs.

maya: noted. Also seeing errors when running the perf script with quantized model: `RuntimeError: kernel not found for op QLinearMatMul` — any known patches?

sam: that's a missing kernel in the custom runtime for opset12+quant. Quick fix: re-export with opset11 OR use the compatibility shim we checked in yesterday: /infra/onnx_shims/quant_compat.patch (apply at runtime startup). infra-bot can spin a VM with the shim?

infra-bot: VM image rwinf-perf-2025-03 has quant_compat applied. I can provision a test instance in us-west2 if you want. Reply with required GPU (A100/RTX6000) and I'll queue it.

maya: A100 preferred. Please queue; I'll run baseline with pad_alignment=1, continuous_batching=false, batches [1,2,4,8,16], seq_lens [32,128,512].

bench-bot: Noted. Scheduling perf job: job_id=rb-perf-175999.queue. Expected runtime ~45m once instance available. Will post logs to /runs/rb-perf-175999/logs and update thread.

maya: thanks. After baseline can we run quant vs fp16 comparison and capture cost per 1M tokens? I want to include that in the catalog entry.

devon: yes — also capture memory high-water mark (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv`) and tail-lat distribution. For profiling, add `--profile torch` to the perf script to get op-level breakdown.

sam: small CI note — once tokenizer checksum is added to metadata.json, the exporter will bundle tokenizer into weights tar. If you want to avoid republishing weights, you can upload tokenizer artifacts separately and set `tokenizer_uri` in metadata to the s3 path.

maya: uploading tokenizer to s3 now at s3://redwood-models/icarus/6b/tokenizer/v1/tokenizer.tar.gz. Updated metadata with checksum and tokenizer_uri. Pushed new metadata to s3 and kicked exporter to repackage.

bench-bot: job rb-perf-175999 starting on instance rwinf-perf-a100-12. Will stream logs to https://logs.redwood.ai/rb-perf-175999 :rocket:

devon: once you have raw numbers please paste p50/p90/p99 and tokens/sec per batch size into the catalog PR. Keep the perf config used as a gist so others can reproduce.

maya: will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: nice. If the leading-space token persists after bundling, we should add a tiny tokenizer regression test to the model onboarding pipeline (one-liner asserting token sequence for 'Hello world').

maya: adding that test to onboarding CI now.

bench-bot: rb-perf-175999 completed. Summary: baseline (cont_batch=false, pad_align=1): p50=43ms p90=78ms p99=192ms at batch=1 seq=32; tokens/sec at batch=8 seq=128 = 18.4k. Full logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/rb-perf-175999/logs.txt

maya: grabbing logs and will open catalog PR with numbers and artifacts. Closing this thread when PR is up.

arjun: great work — ping me on the PR for config linting.

maya: will do.
